description:
FILED s468be (Opus) while attributing the companion ROW DIFF.  Every part of
this is PRE-EXISTING; #1032 made it VISIBLE, the s435/s438h pattern again.

BEFORE (main 73edcff and earlier): t/op/closure.t came back 273 ok / 3 not ok
and died at `aborted-forms:1: Undefined subroutine &main::ff called`.  The
site is t/op/closure.t:661

    sub f { my $x; format ff = ... }
    { fileno ff; write ff; ... }

â a BAREWORD FILEHANDLE in a `fileno` / `write` slot, which is exactly what
#1032 fixed (`%define-fh-slot-op`, and `p-write` was the 44th handle-taking
builtin the audit found).  Perl's rows 271-276 were therefore all `(missing)`.

AFTER (main 0e7c5e3 and today): 274 ok / 7 not ok.  Rows 272 ("cloneable with
eval") and 275 (a `# TODO` row) now PASS â they are the 2 FIXED ROW entries in
the s466/s468be ROW DIFF, and the only reason the file's row baseline moved.
Three rows now fail honestly and one is still lost:

  271  "don't copy a stale lexical; create a fresh undef one instead"
       â the write()/format gap (not-supported.md Â§format / write; the same
       `Undefined subroutine &main::formline` that bounds t/op/write.t).
  273  "cloneable with use re eval"     `push @s, sub { use re 'eval'; my $x;
  274  "cloneable with //ee"             s/$x/1/ } for 1,2; isnt($s[0],$s[1])`
       â an `isnt` on two anon subs made in the same loop: PCL hands back the
       SAME code ref where perl clones per iteration when the body could
       contain an eval (PL_cv_has_eval).  Note row 272, the plain `eval '1'`
       spelling, PASSES â so PCL clones some bodies and not others; that
       asymmetry is the thing to probe first.
  276  "cloning closure proto with no CvOUTSIDE" â still MISSING, and the
       cause is NOT in this file: closure.t:721 is
       `do "./op/closure_test.pl"`, and that file's header comment contains a
       U+2019.  PCL's `do FILE` path chokes on the byte where the file-mode
       path does not â filed and minimised as **#1084**.  It is the file's
       whole remaining shortfall (I2 row t/op/closure.t 6 -> 1) and its whole
       remaining abort (`PCL: cannot parse (inline code): PPI failed to
       tokenize it`).

NOT A REGRESSION: 273/3 -> 274/7 is +1 passing row and 4 rows that stopped
being invisible.  Blessed s468be with this number as the cause.

REPRODUCERS (probe each against perl 5.40.3 before fixing):
  perl -e 'my @s; push @s, sub { use re "eval"; my $x; s/$x/1/ } for 1,2;
           print $s[0]==$s[1] ? "same\n" : "different\n"'      # perl: different
  perl -e 'my @s; push @s, sub { s/1/1/ee } for 1,2;
           print $s[0]==$s[1] ? "same\n" : "different\n"'      # perl: different

PROBED s468be (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl on 9bee19b), all three spellings:
  sub { eval "1" }                  perl: different   PCL: different  (row 272, passes)
  sub { use re "eval"; ... s/$x/1/} perl: different   PCL: SAME       (row 273)
  sub { s/1/1/ee }                  perl: different   PCL: SAME       (row 274)

=== DONE (s470bi) â the closure-IDENTITY half; the format/write row is untouched ===
perl's rule, re-measured over nine shapes (scratch/s469bi/p1083/b.pl, perl
5.40.3): a `sub {â¦}` re-evaluated is the SAME code ref unless the body can
COMPILE PERL AT RUNTIME.  `plain`, `my-only`, `s/$x/1/` without the pragma,
`use re "eval"` ALONE, `s///e`, `eval BLOCK` -> same; `eval "1"`, `s///ee`,
`use re "eval"` + a runtime-interpolated pattern -> different.  That is
PL_cv_has_eval.

PCL answered `same` to ALL NINE -- and the six correct answers were an
ACCIDENT: SBCL hoists a lambda with no free lexical variable into a constant,
so two evaluations are one object.  That accident is exactly why the whole
`different` half was missed (t/op/closure.t rows 273/274 are `isnt` on two subs
made in one loop).

CLASSIFIER `Pl::Parser2::_anon_compiles_at_runtime`, beside the anon-sub
lowering that already walks the block.  Three events: a string `eval` (an
`eval` Word not followed by a Block -- the same test the `:string-eval` scan
makes); `s///ee`, counted from the token's TRAILING MODIFIER LETTERS because
PPI's `get_modifiers` collapses `ee` to `e => 1` (probed); and `use re 'eval'`
lexically in force AND a pattern built at run time -- BOTH required, each alone
is `same` in perl.

A NESTED `sub {â¦}` is NOT excluded, and that is MEASURED, not assumed:
`sub { sub { my $q = sub { eval "1" }; 2 } }` is DIFFERENT in perl (the outer
must hand back a fresh inner each time) while the same shape with `sub { 1 }`
inside stays SAME.  The first version excluded nested subs and got both wrong.

WRAPPER `p-cloned-sub` in the runtime.  A closure is distinct from another
closure only if it actually CLOSES over something, and the obvious cheap trick
does NOT work -- measured in SBCL: `(let ((c (list nil))) (lambda () (progn c
1)))` is EQ to itself (the dead reference is deleted and the lambda re-hoisted)
while `(lambda () c)` is not.  So the wrapper closes over the lambda it calls.
Cost -- one funcall and one &rest list per call -- is paid only by subs that
already pay a runtime transpile, and the calling convention passes through
(guarded by a row: @_, wantarray, and the frame's return).

BARS: corpus-diff 6 of 111 (closure.t + eval.t are this change; every hunk read
and every one a `p-cloned-sub` around an eval-bodied anon sub), silent drops
unchanged; emission-ab RCDIFF 0 with every `cloned+N` file attributed; gate
green.  GUARD `Pl/t/closure-01.t` 25 -> 30 rows, all expectations perl's own
output, inverse-verified against main (exactly the two clone rows fail there).

PROBED AND FILED, NOT FIXED: **#1120** -- `s///ee` behaves as `s///e`.  The
second `e` must evaluate the first evaluation's RESULT as perl code:
`s/(\d)/'$1+1'/ee` gives `$1+1` where perl gives 4.  This task's guard row
asserts the CLONE, not the value, so it keeps passing when #1120 is fixed.
